The Bengali transliteration lines are written with য for the Sanskrit ya (e.g. যাতযামং); whether the printed edition uses য় here is slightly uncertain, and the sentence-level fidelity of the long purport should be spot-checked.
The word-meanings list has 13 entries but the verse's Sanskrit has 12 words (deva-dvija-guru-prājña forms one compound; entries were kept as given, 1:1).
The transliteration of 'śraddhayā parayā' was written with 'যা' instead of the correct 'য়া' (শ্রদ্ধয়া পরয়া); the 'wordMeanings' words carry the same flaw and should be fixed.
The translation has a duplicated word 'পরম পরম' that should read 'পরম'; the first transliteration line follows the given 'OMtatsaditi' as ওঁতৎসদিতি.
Line 1 of the transliteration follows the Roman input ("kriyāḥ"), so "ক্রিযাঃ" keeps the input's spelling instead of the usual Bengali form "ক্রিয়াঃ".

findings.msg: purport ¶1: double quotation marks do not match the English

stamp.note: The translation's quotation marks around sat and its word order are slightly uncertain; the English has no quotes around 'sat', which I added in single quotes.

The word-meanings list has 17 entries in the Bengali output but 18 were given ("na u" counted once in the list, both parts merged), the Sanskrit line 2 appears as given ("prepya" kept), and the garbled "Bhaktivedanta s" in the purport was rendered as "ভক্তিবেদান্ত তাৎপর্য" and may need checking.

The English places 'killer of the Keśī demon, master of the senses' after 'tyāga/sannyāsa'; I kept the order but the Bengali rendering of Sanskrit terms (tyāga/sannyāsa, Keśī) spelling is conventional and may merit a check.
Bengali spelling of 'niścayam' (নিশ্চযম্ vs নিশ্চয়ম্) uses a plain য without nukta; confirm the preferred printed form.
The first transliteration line joins 'bhayāt' and 'tyajet' by sandhi (bhayāttyajet); the Bengali conjunct spelling 'ৎ্ত্য' is a possible orthographic doubt.

The first transliteration line (śarīravāṅmanobhiryat...) was rendered with a Bengali 'ৰ' (Assamese ra) in 'ৰ্যৎ' which should be standard Bengali 'র্যৎ'; spelling of this letter should be double-checked.
The word-meaning for 'api' was left as English 'even' by mistake; it should be 'ও' or 'এমনকি'.
The given Roman line has 'kartāca' (likely 'kartā ca'); I transcribed it as 'কর্তা চ' following the standard verse.
The translation phrase 'one kind of work' is rendered loosely, and 'ahaitukam' meaning 'without cause' was kept as given though it does not appear in the translation.
In the translation, the Bengali rendering of 'determination' (ধৃতি) and the phrase 'sustained with steadfastness' were chosen idiomatically and may merit a native check.
The Bengali word chosen for 'determination' (ধৃতি) and for 'illusion' (মোহ) in the translation may deserve a native reader's check.
The transliteration of the avagraha in 'agre.amṛta' was rendered as ঽ following the standard Sanskrit convention; please confirm the printed edition's spelling.
The English translation is syntactically ambiguous; the Bengali follows its wording literally, so the phrasing of the main clause may need a native check.
The phrase about taking a stone from the fire in winter was rendered literally, and a few phrasings in the long purport could be polished.
The translation sentence is long and was reordered to read naturally in Bengali; wording of the first clause is slightly uncertain.
The Bengali rendering of 'power of speech' as 'বাক্‌শক্তি' and the inline Gītā 2.70 quotation wording are slightly uncertain.
Rendering of 'determination' as ধৃতি and the quoted verse translation in the purport are slightly uncertain in wording.
The long single-paragraph purport was rendered in full, but some phrasing (e.g., the aquatic/ocean analogy and 'brahma-bhūta') may merit a native reviewer's check.
The word list has 12 entries, with the first given as 'cittaḥ' and a final 'yat' not in the verse; I kept them as given.
Transliteration follows the given Roman line literally (yotsya, not the usual printed yotsye); the printed Bengali edition may spell this word differently.
The meaning of 'api' was mistakenly left in English in the word meanings (should be 'ও' / 'তবুও').

The word-meanings list has 14 entries but the verse words are fewer; one entry (mām) repeats, and I kept the given 14 entries. Transliteration of the sandhi form 'priyo.asi' used Bengali 'যো' with avagraha-dot as given.
The purport is one very long paragraph with an embedded Sanskrit verse; rendering is complete but a few phrasings may merit review.
The transliteration's avagraha in 'yo.abhyasūyati' was rendered as 'যোঽভ্যসূয়তি'; the exact printed spelling is slightly uncertain.
The first transliteration line has a possible stray joiner character in 'অনসূয়শ্চ' and the Bengali spelling of the sandhi 'শুভাঁল্লোকান্' may differ slightly from printed editions.

The word-meanings list has 15 entries but the Sanskrit shows 14 words ('arjunaḥ uvāca' counted as one in the verse); I output 14 entries merging per the list's own item 1 — please verify the count against the input list.
The English purport contains a corrupted character in the name Kṛṣṇa in the last sentence, which I rendered as কৃষ্ণ.
The purport's final sentence is garbled in the source ("Bhaktivedanta s to"); I rendered it as a closing colophon with "তাৎপর্য" inferred.
